controls: An uncertainty value is stored or compared with a tier
Require expanded uncertainty at the 95% confidence level rather than an unstated confidence interval.
A normally distributed standard uncertainty is converted to expanded uncertainty
Apply a 1.96 coverage factor, commonly rounded to 2 sigma, and retain the convention used.
Treating one standard deviation as 95% coverage
Use the highest achievable accuracy and treat a lower tier as an exception requiring justification.
The required higher tier is claimed to be infeasible or unreasonably costly
Provide regulator evidence before applying the next lower tier.
A new monitoring plan is submitted
Include an uncertainty assessment demonstrating applicable Annex II, IV or VIII tier compliance.
Approving a plan without tier evidence
A proposed monitoring-plan change affects an applied tier
Refresh and submit the uncertainty assessment with the change.
Major or minor source-stream activity data are reported
Retain evidence that applicable activity-data uncertainty thresholds are met.
Publishing activity data without tier support
Calculation factors for a major or minor source stream are determined
Retain evidence for the uncertainty method or analytical route used for each factor.
Demonstrate compliance with the uncertainty requirements applicable to the measurement system.
Treating CEMS output as inherently compliant
A fall-back methodology covers any part of an installation
Demonstrate the required uncertainty over total installation emissions under the Article 22 route.
Assessing only isolated instruments under a fall-back method
Uncertainty calculations support an annual report
Retain evidence showing that inputs and assumptions remain valid for verifier review.
Losing the audit trail behind tier compliance
Use the quantity over the full scheme year, which is the calendar year.
Activity data are determined for a calculation-based source stream
Use continual process metering or aggregate separately metered deliveries with relevant stock changes.
Delivered quantities are adjusted for inventory
Include uncertainty from beginning- and end-period stock determination unless a valid simplification applies.
A full activity-data uncertainty assessment is required
Account for instrument uncertainty, calibration, practical installation conditions and environmental effects.
Using only the manufacturer headline value
Combustion-fuel activity data are classified as tier 1
Require maximum annual uncertainty below plus or minus 7.5%.
Combustion-fuel activity data are classified as tier 2
Require maximum annual uncertainty below plus or minus 5.0%.
Combustion-fuel activity data are classified as tier 3
Require maximum annual uncertainty below plus or minus 2.5%.
Combustion-fuel activity data are classified as tier 4
Require maximum annual uncertainty below plus or minus 1.5%.
Both operator and third-party measurement systems are available
Prefer the operator-controlled system unless the alternative route is evidenced as at least equivalent and lower risk.
Defaulting to an opaque supplier meter
A supplier meter is governed by national legal metrological control
Allow the legal-metrology route as evidence of reasonably low measurement uncertainty.
Demanding a full assessment where the legal-control simplification applies
A supplier meter is not under legal metrological control
Require contractual maintenance and calibration controls plus confirmation of applicable uncertainty.
A supplier meter is chosen although an operator meter exists
Require evidence that it meets at least the same tier, is more reliable and is less prone to control risks, with a simplified assessment.
Selecting supplier data for convenience only
Uncertainty is assigned to a measurement system
Include measuring instruments, sampling equipment, data-processing equipment, probes, flow meters and telemetry that influence the result.
Assessing a meter while ignoring the supporting system
